patterns.comment: Comment line: * in column 7. Columns 1-5 are the sequence number and column 6 the form type.
patterns.name: comment.line.dds.lf

patterns.comment: Sequence number area, columns 1-5. Not source; scoped as a comment so it recedes visually.
patterns.name: comment.gutter

patterns.comment: Anything past column 80 is ignored by the DDS compiler.
patterns.name: comment.block.line.dds

patterns.comment: Special values such as *ISO or *BLANK. Anchored to the functions area (column 45 onward); a special value cannot appear in the name or attribute columns.
patterns.name: constant.language.dds.lf

patterns.comment: Column 17, the name type. R record format, K key field, J join specification, S select, O omit.
patterns.name: constant.language.dds.lf.nametype

patterns.comment: Column 29: R means the field's attributes come from the file named by REF or REFFLD.
patterns.name: constant.language.dds.lf.ref

patterns.comment: Field length, columns 30-34. A logical file field with no attributes inherits them from the based-on file.
patterns.name: constant.language.dds.lf.len

patterns.comment: Column 35, the data type: P packed, S zoned, B binary, F float, A character, L date, T time, Z timestamp, H hexadecimal, J DBCS-only, E DBCS-either, O DBCS-open, G graphic, 5 (unsigned binary).
patterns.name: constant.language.dds.lf.datatype

patterns.comment: Decimal positions, columns 36-37.
patterns.name: constant.language.dds.lf.decpos

patterns.comment: Column 38, field usage. B both, I input only, N neither (defined but not in the buffer).
patterns.name: constant.language.dds.lf.use

patterns.comment: EDTCDE edit code. Valid codes are 1-4, A-D, J-Q and W-Z, plus 5-9 for user-defined edit codes.
patterns.name: constant.language.dds.lf.edtcde

patterns.comment: REFSHIFT keyboard shift. A, X, W, N, I, D or M for character fields; S, Y, N, I or D for numeric fields.
patterns.name: constant.language.dds.lf.refshift

patterns.comment: Numeric literals in keyword parameters. Anchored to the functions area (column 45 onward), otherwise a digit inside a field name such as #CBX#3 is highlighted as a constant. The length, decimal, indicator and location columns have their own rules.
patterns.name: constant.numeric.dds.lf

patterns.comment: Column 6, the form type. Always A for DDS.
patterns.name: keyword.other.dds.lf.spec

patterns.comment: Continuation character joining this line to the next. Both + and - are valid; + discards the leading blanks of the continuation line and - preserves them. Anchored to end of line so a hyphen or plus inside a keyword parameter is unaffected.
patterns.name: keyword.other.dds.lf

patterns.comment: Keyword set for the functions area. The first lookbehind requires at least 44 characters before the match, so a keyword is found anywhere from column 45 onward and one line may carry several. The second requires the match to begin exactly at column 45 or to follow a non-word character: a plain \b is wrong here, because a keyword starting at column 45 is valid even when column 44 holds a digit, as it does when a position entry abuts the keyword. The trailing boundary stops a keyword matching inside a longer name such as MYGDF.
patterns.name: keyword.other.dds.lf.funcs

patterns.comment: Argument block of a COMP or CMP select/omit comparison. A container rule, so it carries no theme colour of its own; the nested rules scope the operator, the value, and any literal.
patterns.name: dds.lf.comp

patterns.comment: Relational operators for COMP and CMP: EQ, NE, LT, NL, GT, NG, LE, GE.
patterns.name: keyword.other.dds.lf.comp.values

patterns.comment: Numeric literals in keyword parameters, such as RANGE(21 65).
patterns.name: constant.numeric.dds.lf

patterns.comment: Argument block of the CHECK keyword. CHECK accepts a list of edit-check codes, so a lookbehind anchored to CHECK( would only ever match the first one. A container rule carries no theme colour of its own.
patterns.name: dds.lf.check

patterns.comment: CHECK edit-check codes: AB, ME, MF, M10, M11, VN and VNE. M10 and M11 are listed before M1 -prefixed alternatives so the longer code wins.
patterns.name: constant.language.dds.lf.check

patterns.comment: Hexadecimal constant, X'hhhh'. Must be tried before the plain quoted literal so the X prefix is included in the token rather than left unscoped.
patterns.name: string.other.dds.lf.hex

patterns.comment: Continuation character ending an unterminated literal. DDS discards it and joins the lines, so it is not part of the literal's value. Anchored to end of line, so a hyphen or plus inside the text is unaffected.
patterns.name: keyword.other.dds.lf
